scope: Theorem 1.2 (Explicit noiseless precision bound) of the manuscript “Subsphere methods for memory-sample lower bounds in noiseless Gaussian regression” (preprints/Subsphere-methods-for-memory-sample-lower-bounds-in-noiseless-Gaussian-regression-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a645c0aa5ef45578), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let M : N → Z≥0 satisfy M(d) = o(d2). There is a dimension threshold depending only on this memory sequence such that, for every larger d, every 0 < ϵ ≤ 1/10, and every learner in Definition 1.1, the following implication holds. If S is uniform on Sd−1, independently of the Gaussian rows and learner randomness, and P{arccos⟨b s, S⟩ ≤ ϵ} ≥ 2 3 , then T ≥ 2−16 d log2(1/ϵ). (1)
